messages:
aria nguyen: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a small canary for the auth routing change in staging. Policy: prefer project-scoped API key -> fallback to org-scoped key if project missing. Rolling window 10% traffic for 45m. :eyes:

jordan lee: Nice. Can you paste the routing snippet so I can review the telemetry wiring?

aria nguyen: Sure — here's the policy we're applying in the gateway config:
```yaml
routing.auth_priority:
  - project_key
  - org_key
fallback_behavior: 'emit_metric_and_use_org'
metric_labels: ["auth.path", "decision"]
canary.percent: 10
```

maria: Quick question — if a request has an invalid project key but valid org key, do we log that as a failure for the project or success (org)? We need that split for quota and SLA billing.

aria nguyen: Good catch. Current plan: emit two metrics — auth.decision.project_fallback (counter) + auth.success.org (counter). We'll attribute billing to org by default when fallback happens, but flag the project in logs. Telemetry team asked for both signals.

samir: How will console surface this to users? If their project keys start failing because they forgot to add project binding, support will blow up.

aria nguyen: Console change is minimal for canary: a banner on the project Keys page saying "Project key routing canary active — check key binding" with a link to docs. Full UI rollouts are planned later. But we will add a per-project metric in the dashboard: project.auth.fallback_rate.

jordan lee: On quotas — does fallback bypass project quotas? If we attribute billing to org, project quota enforcement could be inconsistent.

aria nguyen: For now, enforcement is evaluated at the decision point: project quota check runs first; if it fails due to 'no project key' we don't reject — we attempt org path. That means project quotas won't block org fallback. We flagged this as a follow-up: project quota strict mode (reject-on-missing) behind feature-flag.

maria: Can we add a sampling trace for fallback cases? e.g., trace_id + reason so SRE can debug routing surprises.

aria nguyen: Yes — added: sample_rate=0.01 for fallback traces. Logs will include reason: missing_project_key | invalid_project_key | quota_block.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy started for routing-service to staging (canary: 10%) — build ci/48219 — invoked by aria nguyen

samir: Will the rollout include a telemetry dashboard link in the canary announcement slack message? Helps support triage.

aria nguyen: Yep — I'm going to post an announcement in #support and #eng-runtime with the dashboard link and grafana panels: auth.decision.* and project.auth.fallback_rate. Also adding a short runbook: how to toggle canary and check sampled traces.

jordan lee: LGTM. If we see a spike in fallback_rate -> revert canary and open an incident. :thumbsup:

aria nguyen: Agreed. I'll monitor the first 45m and report back here with metrics. Thanks all.
